stereoscopic.options.group.name: Stereoscopic
stereoscopic.options.mode.name: Mode
stereoscopic.options.mode.tooltip: Selects the stereoscopic output mode. SBS Half splits the framebuffer left/right at half horizontal resolution per eye, for displays that stretch each half back to full width (3D TVs/monitors, VR virtual-monitor passthrough). SBS Full renders each eye at per-eye (W/2)/H aspect so each half is proportionally correct with no display stretch — for double-wide desktops (e.g. 3840x1080) and full-SBS 3D inputs.
stereoscopic.options.ipd.name: IPD (meters)
stereoscopic.options.ipd.tooltip: Interpupillary distance / stereo strength — the horizontal eye separation used to compute per-eye camera offset. Default 0.064 m matches the human-average IPD (real humans are ~55–77 mm). Values above ~77 mm are hyperstereo: exaggerated depth / stronger SBS pop, not anatomically realistic. Max 100 mm.
stereoscopic.options.convergence.name: Convergence distance
stereoscopic.options.convergence.tooltip: Off-axis convergence depth in blocks. Objects at this depth sit at the screen plane (zero parallax); closer objects pop out, farther ones recede. 0 = parallel-axis (no shear, everything pops out).
stereoscopic.options.swap_eyes.name: Swap eyes
stereoscopic.options.swap_eyes.tooltip: Flip which eye's render goes to which physical eye. Toggle if depth appears inverted (objects look behind the screen when they should pop out, or vice versa), or if reflections look like they're for the opposite eye on your SBS display / VR passthrough setup.
